questions.question: Three statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some desks are trays. Some trays are plates. Some plates are desks. Conclusions: I. All desks are plates. II. All plates are desks. III. Some plates are trays. IV. All trays are desks.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some desks are trays.

Some trays are plates.

Some plates are desks.

Conclusions:

I. All desks are plates.

II. All plates are desks.

III. Some plates are trays.

IV. All trays are desks.
questions.solution:
I. All desks are plates. → Does not follow (As, Some plates are desks → desks are plates)

II. All plates are desks. → Does not follow (As, Some plates are desks)

III. Some plates are trays. → Follows (As, Some trays are plates)

IV. All trays are desks. → Does not follow (As, Some desks are trays → trays are desks)

Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation.

256 * 4 * 9 * 3 * 14 = 51
questions.solution:
4. ÷ − × +

256 ÷ 4 - 9 × 3 + 14 = 51

⇒ 64 - 27 + 14 = 51

⇒ 78 - 27 = 51

⇒ 51 = 51

Hence, '÷ − × +' is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following is used as a cooling medium for the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the superconducting magnets in MRI scanners and NMR spectrometers?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is used as a cooling medium for the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the superconducting magnets in MRI scanners and NMR spectrometers?
questions.solution: Helium is used as a cooling medium for the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the superconducting magnets in MRI scanners and NMR spectrometers due to its ability to remain in a liquid state at extremely low temperatures. In the LHC, helium is used to cool the superconducting magnets to temperatures close to absolute zero (-273.15°C) in order to maintain their superconductivity. In MRI scanners and NMR spectrometers, helium is used to cool the superconducting coils which create the strong magnetic fields needed for imaging.

questions.question: Ryotwari system of revenue collection in India, introduced by the British, was based on the _______.
questions.questionHtml: Ryotwari system of revenue collection in India, introduced by the British, was based on the _______.
questions.solution: The Ryotwari system of revenue collection in India was introduced by the British during their colonial rule. This system was based on the Ricardian theory of rent, which states that rent is the surplus income earned by landowners due to the differential fertility of land. Under the Ryotwari system, individual farmers or ryots were directly responsible for paying land revenue to the government.

questions.questionHtml: The marked price of mustard oil is 25% more than its cost price. At what percentage less than the marked price should it be sold to have no profit and no loss?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price of mustard oil be Rs 100x.

Marked price = 100x + 25x = 125x

For no profit, no loss, Selling price = Rs 100x

Discount percentage offered on MP = ((125x - 100x) / 125x) × 100 ⇒ 20%

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 25 days while B can complete the same work in 30 days. They work on alternate basis, starting with A. Both A and B follow this pattern for 5 days and then A leaves the work. In how many days will B finish the remaining work?
questions.questionHtml: A can complete a piece of work in 25 days while B can complete the same work in 30 days. They work on alternate basis, starting with A. Both A and B follow this pattern for 5 days and then A leaves the work. In how many days will B finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Total work = LCM of (25, 30) = 150 unit

The efficiency of A = 150/25 = 6 unit/day

The efficiency of B = 150/30 = 5 unit/day

A and B work alternatively for 5 days, starting with A ⇒ 6 × 3 + 5 × 2 = 28 unit

Remaining work = 150 - 28 = 122

The Time taken by B to complete the remaining work = 122/5 = 24(2/5) days

questions.questionHtml: If \(7 b-\frac{1}{4 b}=7\), then what is the value of \(16 b^2+\frac{1}{49 b^2}\) ?
questions.solution:
Multiplying the expression by 4/7.

⇒  4/7 × (7b - 1/4b) = 7 × 4/7 ⇒  4b - 1/7b = 4

Squaring both sides:

⇒ (4b - 1/7b)2 = 42 ⇒ \(16 b^2+\frac{1}{49 b^2}\)- 2 × 4 × 1/7 = 16 ⇒ \(16 b^2+\frac{1}{49 b^2}\) = 120/7

questions.question: Two runners, Sony and Mony, start running on a circular track of length 200 m at speeds of 18 and 24 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. After how much time from the start will they meet again at the starting point?
questions.questionHtml: Two runners, Sony and Mony, start running on a circular track of length 200 m at speeds of 18 and 24 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. After how much time from the start will they meet again at the starting point?
questions.solution:
The relative speed of both in the same direction = S2 - S1 ⇒ 24 - 18 ⇒ 6 km/h ⇒ 6 * (5/18) = 5/3 m/s.

Time taken by them to meet for the first time at the starting point on the track while running in the same direction = (Length of track / Relative speed in the same direction)

= 200/(5/3) ⇒ 120 seconds

questions.question: What will be the remainder when (265) 4081 + 9 is divided by 266?

questions.solution:
Calculation:

(265)4081 + 9 is divisible by 266

⇒ (266 - 1)4081+ 9

Now when divided by 266, 

⇒ \( (266 - 1)^{4081}\over 266\) + \(9 \over 266\)

Remainder from first fraction will be (- 1)4081and + 9 from second fraction

Remainder as whole = - 1 + 9 = 8

∴ Remainder when (265)4081+ 9 is divided by 266 is 8.

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. He repeated the experiment, increasing the amount until he had weighed up to a thousand pounds.

B. During the spring of 1717, the iron foundries in a remote district were often visited by a thin, middle-aged man with a notebook.

C. Three cauldrons were next prepared under his directions.

D. He would weigh out two pounds of iron, have them heated till they were red-hot and then weigh them again.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "BDAC."

Key Points

  •  The paragraph is about a middle-aged man visiting iron foundries and conducting an experiment.
    • ​Thus, we will place sentence B at the beginning of the passage.
  • Further, sentence D explains what the man used to do in the iron foundaries.
  • Sentence A further explains how he repeated the experiment with increasing amounts of iron until he reached a thousand pounds.
  • Sentence C finally explains how three cauldrons were prepared under his directions.
  • Thus, it can be concluded that the correct order for the given sentences should be "BDAC."

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Key Points

  • This structure is used to compare two things that have the same level of the quality described by the adjective.

  • In this case, we are comparing the woman's beauty to that of a peacock.
  • The sentence could be rephrased as "She is as beautiful as a peacock in the blue satin saree."

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. The hunter dogs followed the hyena’s ________.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank.

The hunter dogs followed the hyena’s ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "scent."

Key Points

  • Homonym is a word that is spelt and pronounced like another word but that has a different meaning.
    • Example: ‘Bank’ [river bank] and ‘bank’ [place where money is kept] are homonyms.
  • Now, let us understand the meaning of the given options:
    • "Sense" means common sense or good judgment.
    • "Scent" means an odor or trail, whereas "sense" means a feeling or perception.
    • "Cense" means to burn incense, which is not relevant to the context of the sentence.
    • "Cents" refers to a unit of currency, which does not make sense in the context of the sentence.
  • In the given sentence, the word "scent" will fit the best.
  • The correct sentence will be: The hunter dogs followed the hyena’s scent.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Hinglish

  • "Scent" का मतलब होता है एक सुगंध या ट्रेल (मार्ग), जबकि "sense" का मतलब होता है एक भावना या अनुभूति।

The correct answer is "considered."
 Key Points
  • "Considered" is the past participle form of the verb "consider," which is the most appropriate tense to use in this context.
  • The sentence is discussing a past action, so the past participle form is necessary.
  • Using "considering" (present participle) or "to consider" (infinitive) would not be grammatically correct in this sentence.
  • "Consider" on its own is not a past tense or participle form, and therefore does not fit the context of the sentence.
  • The phrase "Human life is considered a unique blessing" uses "considered" to indicate an opinion or perspective on human life.
  • This choice smoothly connects the subject "Human life" with the predicate "a unique blessing," forming a complete, grammatically correct sentence that conveys a general view. 

Additional Information

  • "Considering" is a present participle form of the verb "consider." It would be appropriate to use in a sentence discussing a current action or ongoing process.
  • "To consider" is an infinitive form of the verb "consider." It would be appropriate to use in a sentence discussing a future action or intention.
  • "Consider" on its own is the base form of the verb and does not fit the past tense context of the sentence.

The correct answer is "As a result."
 Key Points
  • "As a result" is the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4 as it indicates a consequence or outcome of the previous statement.
  • Grammatically, "as a result" is a conjunction that connects two clauses, with the first clause stating the cause and the second clause stating the effect.
    • Example: "I forgot my keys at home, as a result, I had to call my roommate to let me in."

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 1".
